templates.stem: Draw the straight line through $A({=x1}, {=y1})$ and $B({=x2}, {=y2})$.
solution: Find the gradient between A and B: m = (y2 − y1) / (x2 − x1).
Keep the sign of each difference exactly as it comes out — do not drop a sign when a coordinate is already negative.
Starting from A, step according to that gradient (rise over run) to fix the line's direction.
Any two points lying on this same line are an acceptable construction — it is the line itself that is graded, not the two named points.
templates.notes: Tests the geometric core of LO1 (the unique line two points determine) rather than the symbolic y = mx + c form; graded on the property (any two collinear points are correct, FR-1205). Anchor ex8-6-10a's own points (A(-6,1)) fall outside the instrument's ±5 lattice limit, so instance parameters were rescaled to the same gradient family (1/3) while two further instances stress negative coordinates and a whole-number gradient. intercept-wrong and vertical-line are valid predicates for this kind but have no clean, non-strained match among this LO's own misconceptions, so they are left undiagnosed rather than forced.

templates.stem: Line $L$ has equation $y = {=linear(m0, b0)}$. Draw the line through the point $({=px}, {=py})$ that is {=relation} to $L$.
solution: Read the gradient of L from its equation (the coefficient of x).
Apply the rule for the relationship asked: parallel keeps the same gradient; perpendicular takes the negative reciprocal.
Substitute the given point's coordinates into y = mx + c with the new gradient and solve for c.
Draw the line with that gradient through the given point (or any other point lying on it).
templates.notes: Tests the 'use the relationship to find the equation of a line' half of LO2. Verified numerically for both instances (reference gradients 2 and -3, neither ±1) that applying the wrong relationship produces a gradient matching neither slope-inverted nor slope-sign-flipped against the true target, so it lands cleanly on off-target — mapped to this LO's own swaps-parallel-perpendicular-tests, the likeliest error and the one this construction most specifically reveals. The remaining predicates surface LO1 prerequisite slips (own=false) that a construction can't tell apart from a genuine relationship confusion once only the resulting line is observed. vertical-line has no match here. This LO's other three misconceptions (judges-parallel-by-appearance, stops-at-partial-quadrilateral-property, and swaps-parallel-perpendicular-tests read as a classification act rather than a construction act) describe judging an already-given relationship or shape, not drawing a fresh line — see the filed gap for this LO.

gaps.description: A widget showing two already-drawn line segments (or a quadrilateral's four vertices) on a lattice, where the student builds the comparison itself — e.g. exposing each segment's own rise-over-run and then classifying the pair as parallel, perpendicular, or neither, or for a quadrilateral, checking each side-pair in turn — rather than drawing one new line. This would diagnose: calling sides parallel/perpendicular from how the sketch looks rather than the computed gradients (judges-parallel-by-appearance); confirming only one defining property of a quadrilateral and stopping there instead of checking the second the book pairs with it (stops-at-partial-quadrilateral-property); and blurring the parallel test (equal gradients) with the perpendicular test (product of exactly -1) when reading the comparison (swaps-parallel-perpendicular-tests, as a judgement rather than a construction error).
gaps.why: line_drawer only grades one freshly-drawn line's own slope and intercept against a single target; it has no mechanism for a student to compare two already-given gradients or classify a pre-drawn shape's sides, so these three misconceptions (all about mis-judging an existing relationship, not about drawing a new line) have no home. polygon_builder's construct mode is graded on the shape the student itself builds, not on classifying a pre-drawn one, so it does not fit either without inverting the whole interaction. treats-contradiction-as-a-k-value (recognising an equation with no solution) is purely algebraic and fits no visual construction kind at all.

gaps.description: A widget presenting three points on a lattice where the student builds the actual comparison the book teaches — either the two gradients between consecutive point-pairs (confirming or denying they are the exact same fraction), or the two shorter segment lengths against the longest (confirming or denying they sum to it) — rather than drawing any single line. This would diagnose: treating two gradients that merely share a sign as equal instead of checking they are the same fraction exactly (same-sign-gradients-mistaken-for-equal); and leaving distances as separate, un-simplified surds so a genuine match is missed and the points are wrongly called non-collinear (unsimplified-surds-look-unequal).
gaps.why: Collinearity is a three-point equality judgement, not the construction of one line. line_drawer mode='points' only grades whether the drawn line passes through two given points and never involves or grades a third, so building it here would just re-test LO1's two-point-line skill under a different name rather than this LO's actual comparison step — the stretch the rules warn against. No other listed kind offers a multi-value numeric-equality comparison interaction (gradient-vs-gradient or surd-length-vs-surd-length).

records.notes: Lesson g10m8s3-2 (Chapter 8, Analytical geometry) has three objectives. Two get genuine line_drawer templates (equation of a line through two points; parallel/perpendicular construction), keeping the lesson's widget count at 2 as expected ("usually zero to two"). The third (collinearity) is a clean gap: it is an equality judgement across three points that no listed kind's grading model supports. A supplementary gap is also filed against the parallel/perpendicular objective for the three of its four misconceptions that describe judging an already-given relationship/shape rather than constructing a fresh line — the template covers the objective's construction half honestly but does not cover that other half, and forcing it would have meant stretching line_drawer's predicates past what they actually detect. Read only the three files named in the task plus the one figure (tikzpicture__210f1cf26efb7f7004269fa6b030bf75.png) needed to confirm anchor ex8-6-10a's point data before designing around it; that anchor's own points fall outside the line_drawer lattice limit (±5), so template instances use rescaled numbers carrying the same gradient family instead of the anchor's literal values.
